brief: September CPI ran hot: headline +0.6% m/m (from 0.4%), core +0.3% for a second straight month above the 0.2% consensus, annual rate to 2.6% from 2.4%, with breadth beyond energy. Equities fell and October hike odds rose to ~40% from ~20%. UBS now expects Fed hikes in December and March (two more, versus market pricing of 3.5) and raised its end-December 10-year Treasury yield forecast to 4.9% from 4.6%, still below Wednesday's 5.19% close, leaving room for yields to fall if the Fed waits and data cool. UBS argues growth (GDP near 2.5-3%), a resilient labor market, ISM expansion, and a strong earnings season (28% S&P 500 EPS growth, AI capex +84% to USD 900bn) let equities absorb higher rates, citing average 10.8% S&P 500 gains in the year after past Fed hiking starts. Separately: Germany is pushing the EU toward wider China trade safeguards after a record trade surplus, which UBS says doesn't warrant de-risking; and TSMC's record Q3 profit and strong Q4 guide reinforce UBS's constructive AI view despite recent chip-stock weakness.
